key_insight: The study generates healthy-looking mammograms by inpainting lesions out of abnormal images, using these counterfactuals to improve breast cancer classifier training.
clinical_relevance: This augmentation approach may help CAD systems miss fewer cancers by boosting sensitivity while keeping false positives controlled.
method: Train a diffusion model on BI-RADS 1 healthy mammograms.
Use RePaint-based inpainting inside lesion bounding boxes to replace lesions with realistic normal tissue.
Augment four classifiers: ConvNeXt, ViT, Mammo-CLIP, and FPN-MIL.
evidence_signal: On the VinDr-Mammo dataset, the generated counterfactuals improved sensitivity across all evaluated models, especially at 80% fixed specificity, and radiologists judged the realism consistent with the source data.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on accurate lesion annotations and high-quality synthetic inpainting, so real-world robustness and generalization still need careful validation.
paper_title: Healthy Counterfactual Generation via Diffusion Inpainting for Mammography Classification
